newsitem.title: USA: USWC gasolines rise on strike threat, tight supply.
newsitem.headline: USWC gasolines rise on strike threat, tight supply.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices were up sharply midday Thursday, as refineries geared up after maintenance shutdowns and workers threatened to strike at four California facilities, traders said.

The union representing workers at Unocal's California refineries on Wednesday threatened to terminate its contract, setting the stage for the disruption of 250,000 barrels-per-day of light products production.
CARB gasoline in Los Angeles was talked 2.50 cents gallon higher Thursday at 82 to 83 cents, traders said.
Conventional grade rose 1.50 cents to 79/80 cents.
The threat of a strike comes amid reports of low inventory data. West Coast gasoline inventories fell 1.2 million barrels last week to 25.7 million.
In San Francisco, CARB gasoline rose 1.50 cents a gallon to 80/81 cents on Thursday.
Distillates were narrowly mixed, with low sulphur diesel up a half cent to 79/80 cents, and CARB diesel notional lower at 75/76 cents.
